question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2023 Q1b — Average, Moles, and Salt Mass
question.text:
Use the titration results to answer the following. The concordant titration volumes (Titrations 2 and 3) were both 25.0 cm³.

Reagents:

  • Sulfuric acid: concentration 4.9 g dm⁻³, molar mass 98 g mol⁻¹
  • Sodium hydroxide: 5 g dissolved in 250 cm³
  • Balanced equation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O

R.A.M.: Na = 23, O = 16, S = 32
question.general_feedback:
(iii) Average volume: Both concordant titrations gave 25.0 cm³ → average = 25.0 cm³

(vi) Moles of H₂SO₄:
Concentration in mol/dm³ = 4.9 ÷ 98 = 0.05 mol dm⁻³
Volume = 25.0 cm³ = 0.025 dm³
Moles = 0.05 × 0.025 = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol

(vii) Mass of Na₂SO₄:
From equation: moles Na₂SO₄ = moles H₂SO₄ = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol
Molar mass Na₂SO₄ = 2(23) + 32 + 4(16) = 142 g mol⁻¹
Mass = 1.25 × 10⁻³ × 142 = 0.1775 g ≈ 0.18 g

steps.label:
Given: Concordant volumes: T2 = T3 = 25.0 cm³  |  H₂SO₄: 4.9 g dm⁻³, M = 98 g mol⁻¹
Formulas: c (mol dm⁻³) = mass concentration ÷ molar mass    n = c × V    mass = n × M
Equation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O (mole ratio 1:1 for H₂SO₄:Na₂SO₄)
Part (iii) — Calculate the average volume of sulfuric acid used. (1 mark)
Part (vi) — Calculate the number of moles of H₂SO₄ used. (2 marks)
Part (vii) — Calculate the mass of Na₂SO₄ (normal salt) expected. (3 marks)

fields.label: Average volume of H₂SO₄ = _____ cm³
fields.diagnostic_hint: Both concordant titrations (T2 and T3) gave 25.0 cm³ → average = (25.0 + 25.0) / 2 = 25.0 cm³

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Only use the concordant (agreeing) titrations to calculate the average — not the rough titration. Here T2 = T3 = 25.0 cm³, so the average = 25.0 cm³.

fields.label: Concentration of H₂SO₄ = _____ mol dm⁻³
fields.diagnostic_hint: c (mol dm⁻³) = mass concentration ÷ molar mass = 4.9 ÷ 98 = 0.05 mol dm⁻³

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Concentration in mol/dm³ = g/dm³ ÷ g/mol = 4.9 ÷ 98 = 0.05 mol dm⁻³.
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Convert g/dm³ to mol/dm³ by dividing by molar mass. c = 4.9 g dm⁻³ ÷ 98 g mol⁻¹ = 0.05 mol dm⁻³.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: n = c × V. Convert volume: 25.0 cm³ = 0.025 dm³. Then n = 0.05 × 0.025 = 0.00125 mol.
error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Did you convert cm³ to dm³? Divide by 1000: 25.0 cm³ ÷ 1000 = 0.025 dm³.

fields.label: Moles of Na₂SO₄ produced = _____ mol
fields.diagnostic_hint: From H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄: mole ratio H₂SO₄ : Na₂SO₄ = 1:1. So moles Na₂SO₄ = moles H₂SO₄ = 0.00125 mol

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Check the balanced equation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. The mole ratio of H₂SO₄ to Na₂SO₄ is 1:1, so moles of salt = moles of acid.

fields.label: Molar mass of Na₂SO₄ = _____ g mol⁻¹

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: mass = moles × molar mass = 0.00125 × 142 = 0.1775 g. Accept 0.18 g (2 sig figs).
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: mass = n × M. Multiply moles of Na₂SO₄ by its molar mass (142 g/mol).
